title: 3.3. Logic and Bitwise Operations
summary: Combine logical expressions using and, or, not with short-circuit evaluation, and manipulate individual bits using &, |, ~, ^, <<, and >>.
learningObjectives: Evaluate compound conditions with logical operators: and, or, not.

sections.heading: 3.3.1 Boolean Logical Operators & Short-Circuiting
sections.content:
Python provides three logical operators:
• and: True only if BOTH operands are True.
• or: True if AT LEAST ONE operand is True.
• not: Unary negation that inverts truth value.

Python uses short-circuit evaluation: if the left operand of an and is False, the right operand is NEVER evaluated, saving compute and preventing runtime errors.

knowledgeChecks.prompt: What is the result of True or False and False in Python?
knowledgeChecks.explanation: The and operator has higher precedence than or: False and False is False; then True or False evaluates to True.

recap: and requires both operands; or requires one; not negates. and precedes or in operator hierarchy.
